item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 181734
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Sun Oct 18 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Trudy, located offshore of southwestern Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form well offshore of
southern Mexico during the next day or two. Environmental
conditions appear conducive for gradual development thereafter, and
a tropical depression is likely to form around the middle of this
week while it moves westward to west-northwestward, well south of
Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Public Advisory Number 22
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Sun Oct 18 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 182041
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Trudy Advisory Number  22
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
200 PM MST Sun Oct 18 2026
 
...TRUDY EXPECTED TO RAPIDLY WEAKEN LATER TONIGHT...
...ALL WARNINGS DISCONTINUED FOR THE COAST OF MEXICO AND THE ISLAS
MARIAS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM MST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.5N 107.0W
ABOUT 180 MI...290 KM WNW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 105 MI...170 KM SW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...974 MB...28.77 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The Government of Mexico has discontinued all warnings for the 
coast of Mexico and Las Islas Marias.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:

There are no coastal watches and warnings in effect.
 
Interests in southwestern and west-central Mexico, as well as Baja 
California Sur should continue to monitor the progress of Trudy.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM MST (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Trudy was located
near latitude 19.5 North, longitude 107.0 West. Trudy is moving
toward the northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h). A turn toward the
west-northwest tonight is expected tonight. On the forecast track, 
the center of Trudy will move away from the coast of mainland 
Mexico this afternoon and tonight, then move south of Baja 
California Sur on Monday and Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have weakened to near 100 mph (155 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Rapid weakening is expected to begin tonight, 
and Trudy could degenerate to a post-tropical low by Tuesday night.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles
(150 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 974 mb (28.77 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?key_messages.
 
WIND: Wind gusts to tropical storm force are possible this 
afternoon and this evening over portions of the coast of 
west-central Mexico and Las Islas Marias.
 
RAINFALL: Through tonight, Trudy is expected to produce an 
additional 1 to 4 inches of rain along and near the southwest 
Mexican coast in Jalisco. This rainfall may produce localized flash 
flooding and mudslides, especially in areas along steep terrain.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Trudy, 
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic 
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: Coastal flooding from storm surge should subside along 
the coast of Mexico this afternoon and tonight.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are affecting portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next two to 
three days. These swells will cause life-threatening surf and rip 
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather 
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 22
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Sun Oct 18 2026 
ZCZC MIATCDEP1 ALL
TTAA00 KNHC DDHHMM
 
Hurricane Trudy Discussion Number  22
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
200 PM MST Sun Oct 18 2026

An Air Force Reserve Hurricane Hunter aircraft investigating Trudy 
this afternoon found maximum 700 mb flight-level winds of 95 kt in 
the northeast eyewall, with a dropsonde in that area suggesting 
surface winds of about 85 kt. The minimum central pressure was near 
974 mb. Thus, the initial intensity is lowered to 85 kt.  During 
the last hour or so, the hurricane's cloud pattern has started to 
lose organization, and this is likely a sign of the forecast 
increasing shear and the upcoming weakening trend.
 
The initial motion northwestward at a slower forward speed or 325/5 
kt. A turn toward the west-northwest at an even slower forward 
speed is forecast as Trudy shears apart vertically and becomes 
steered by the lighter low- to mid-level flow. The new forecast 
track is similar to the previous track and lies near the center of 
the guidance envelope. On the forecast track, the hurricane will 
move away from southwest and west-central Mexico this afternoon and 
then move slowly south of Baja California Sur on Monday and Tuesday.

Trudy is starting to encounter increasing southwesterly shear and a 
drier and more stable airmass. The dynamical intensity guidance 
forecasts this combination to cause rapid weakening starting near 
the 12 h point at the latest, and the intensity forecast follows 
the trend of this guidance. The new forecast follows the previous 
forecast in showing Trudy degenerating to a post-tropical cyclone 
by 60 hours and dissipating in 3 or 4 days. Both of these could 
occur sooner than currently predicted.
 
 
KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. Although tropical storm conditions are moving away from the 
Mexican coast, gusts to tropical storm-force are possible this 
afternoon and evening over portions of the coast of west-central 
Mexico and the Islas Marias.
 
2. Coastal flooding due to storm surge should subside this 
afternoon and tonight.
 
3. Heavy rainfall associated with Trudy will continue to impact the 
southwest Mexican coast in Jalisco through tonight. This rainfall 
may produce areas of flooding and mudslides, especially in areas 
along steep terrain.
 
4. Large swells will continue to affect the coast of southwestern
Mexico and west-central Mexico during the next two to three days, 
causing life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 24H  19/1800Z 20.1N 108.0W   65 KT  75 MPH

$$
